title: All proposed routes around the global repeated-halving obstruction
question: do prime-ledger invariance, zero genealogy, real-rooted kernel refinement, or compactified seam control close the RH gap?

verdict.conclusion: all four routes were tested. Each yields a precise sufficient theorem, but the missing step reappears as a nonzero dyadic prime correction, uncontrolled entry from infinity, failure of positive blends to preserve real-rootedness, or the essential singularity at the compactified infinity seam. No route currently supplies the required global coercivity.

primeLedgerRoute.target: derive invariance of the positive central horizontal residue from an exact dyadic identity on the completed prime ledger
primeLedgerRoute.parityIdentity: (1-2^(-s)) zeta(s) removes the even Euler contributions
primeLedgerRoute.consequence: the elementary dyadic/parity operation has a nonzero central curvature correction, so literal halving is not an invariance of the prime ledger
primeLedgerRoute.reservoirProblem: closure may conserve residue plus a carrier or branch reservoir rather than the horizontal residue alone; proving the reservoir returns empty is an additional theorem
primeLedgerRoute.quaternaryProblem: four spectral copies at half displacement conserve quadratic horizontal energy, so the 1000 fork can return the exported norm instead of forcing it to vanish
primeLedgerRoute.status: no prime-side identity deriving R_after=R_before was found

genealogyRoute.localTheorem: for a holomorphic family F(lambda,s), zeros inside any compact zero-free contour continue with multiplicity and cannot be born spontaneously in its interior

localGenealogyExample.consequence: inside a compact contour whose boundary remains zero-free, zeros continue locally under analytic coefficient changes; count changes indicate boundary crossing, not spontaneous interior birth

genealogyRoute.globalFailure: on a noncompact plane, zeros may cross every expanding contour from infinity; the escaping quartet is precisely such a boundary-at-infinity entry
genealogyRoute.orderFailure: uniform finite order or exponential type is insufficient because multiplication by a stage-dependent polynomial preserves order while adding escaping zeros
genealogyRoute.sufficientMissingTheorem: a uniform nonvanishing estimate on an exhaustion of contours, or a regular seam divisor accounting for every incoming zero
genealogyRoute.status: local parentage is automatic, but global no-birth is not established

kernelRoute.target: construct canonical K_N with real-rooted Fourier transforms and strong convergence to the exact Riemann kernel

positiveBlendCounterexample.consequence: both inputs have only real zeros, but their positive half-sum has nonreal zeros because the roots do not interlace

halvingDilation.consequence: composition with 2z preserves real-rootedness and contracts roots, but repeated dilation cannot converge to the fixed xi function; coefficient or kernel averaging needs an interlacing-preservation theorem

kernelRoute.polyaRoute: real-rooted Pólya-like transforms are available, but preserving real-rootedness while converging through the body of the exact Riemann kernel remains open
kernelRoute.status: positivity and halving do not establish Laguerre-Polya membership

compactifiedSeamRoute.positiveResult: the supremum of horizontal displacement remains 1/4 for an escaping quartet and therefore detects what convergent residue sums miss
compactifiedSeamRoute.analyticFailure: xi is a nonpolynomial entire function with infinitely many zeros, so infinity is an essential singularity; it cannot extend holomorphically as a regular point of the Riemann sphere
compactifiedSeamRoute.consequence: topological endpoint identification does not provide analytic seam regularity, and nonholomorphic compactification does not transfer the identity theorem
compactifiedSeamRoute.sufficientMissingTheorem: a new normalized section or divisor on the compactified seam whose norm is coercive in horizontal displacement and whose convergence is uniform at the seam
compactifiedSeamRoute.status: the seam norm detects escape set-theoretically but is not controlled by the current analytic completion

exactProgress: aggregate residue contraction is algebraically exact
local zero genealogy holds on every fixed zero-free contour
a seam supremum detects fixed-displacement escape
blockingFacts: the p=2 dyadic correction is nonzero at the central ledger point
zeros can enter from infinity in a noncompact analytic family
positive sums of real-rooted components need not remain real-rooted
xi has an essential singularity at compactified infinity
four spectral branches at half scale can conserve the residue being contracted
narrowestNextTargets: derive an exact completed-ledger identity cancelling the p=2 correction and every reservoir term
prove interlacing for every canonical theta-carrier refinement
construct a seam divisor that accounts for zeros entering from infinity without requiring xi to be regular there
combinedAssessment.status: all suggested routes remain conditional; no proof of RH is obtained
